cohort: 14,335 women in Sweden, including nulliparous women, primiparous women who had a cesarean delivery, and primiparous women who had a vaginal delivery
finding: Both pregnancy and vaginal delivery were associated with an increased risk of urinary incontinence 20 years later, while cesarean delivery was associated with a reduced risk.
mod_finding: Compared to vaginal delivery, cesarean delivery was associated with a 30% reduction in urinary incontinence and a 35-52% reduction in more severe types of incontinence.
